**Finding: Compliant (preferred position).**

- **Rule:** MFN — most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer (PB).
- **Result:** No MFN obligation on PB exists anywhere in the agreement, satisfying the preferred element "Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor." No redline proposed.
- **Investigation:** Searched for MFN phrasing (most favored nation, no less/at least as favorable, best/lowest price, match, right of first refusal/negotiation, terms offered to any other party). The single instance of "favorable" in the document is p0543.
- **Near-hit dispositioned:** p0543 (Article 7, Security Interest) requires any replacement lender's subordination agreement to be "taken as a whole not less favorable in any material respect to SFJ" than the SVB subordination agreement. That is a baseline-preservation covenant benchmarked to one named instrument for lender-protection purposes — not a duty to extend SFJ any better terms given to third parties, and not a pricing MFN.
- **Also checked:** Section 7.5.5 (p0552) restricting Licensing Transactions operates through SFJ consent (with arbitration on Material Impact), not through disclosure, matching, or best-offer mechanics, so it is outside this rule.
